IA-2025-SF2508.title: A bill for an act modifying the major economic growth attraction program, and including effective date provisions.

actions.text: Introduced, referred to Ways and Means.
Subcommittee: Dawson, Bisignano, Bousselot, Dickey, Dotzler, et al..
Placed on Ways and Means calendar.

IA-2025-SF2508.policyArea: business assistance, major economic growth attraction program, tax credits
IA-2025-SF2508.aiSummary: The bill would change Iowa’s major economic growth attraction program. It would add new rules for where projects must be located, raise the tax credit to up to 10% for one project in a rural county, and let some rural county credits be refundable and transferred to another person with approval. It would also tighten repayment rules if a business breaks program rules and add penalties if a project’s land or buildings are sold, razed, or made unusable within five years.

IA-2025-HCR106.aiSummary: The resolution would set the final adjournment of the 2026 Extraordinary Session of the Iowa General Assembly for Friday, October 2, 2026. It affects the House and Senate and ends that session when they adjourn on that date.

IA-2025-SF654.title: A bill for an act relating to wildlife, including the treatment of beaver dams, identification for traps, snares, and tree stands, maximum fur dealer license fees, and deer depredation, and making penalties applicable.

IA-2025-SF654.aiSummary: Iowa enacted a law on wildlife rules for beaver dams, tree stands, traps, snares, fur dealer licenses, and deer damage permits. It requires ID tags on tree stands on public land, sets rules for tags and checks on traps and snares, and lets owners or drainage districts alter beaver dams to protect property. It also caps fur dealer license fees at $50 a year and keeps deer depredation permits available for landowners or tenants with at least $1,000 in wildlife damage.

IA-2025-SF2490.policyArea: agriculture and land stewardship department, arbitration, confidentiality
IA-2025-SF2490.aiSummary: The law changes Iowa rules for oil and gas production, including filing papers with the Department of Natural Resources, shared drilling plans, and how confidential records are handled. It creates a severance tax account in the Environment First Fund, and money in it is to support water quality projects. It also lets the department set special spacing units for exploratory wells and gives civil penalties for violations.

House concurred in Senate amendment H-8472.
Read first time, referred to Ways and Means.
Introduced, placed on Ways and Means calendar.

IA-2025-HF2765.aiSummary: Iowa law now adds rules for mining land that is affected by subsidence, which means land sinking or collapsing above an underground mine on public land or in a public right-of-way. It directs the state to make rules for reporting these cases, who can file a repair plan, and how soon repairs must be done. The law also says the state must adopt emergency rules within 60 business days after it took effect, and it took effect when it was enacted.

IA-2025-HF2756.title: A bill for an act relating to licensing of service companies, motor vehicle service contracts, and residential service contracts, and providing civil penalties and including effective date provisions.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, passed on file.
Introduced, placed on Ways and Means calendar.

IA-2025-HF2756.aiSummary: Iowa now requires service companies to be licensed before they can sell motor vehicle or residential service contracts in the state. It sets rules for license applications, renewals, reporting changes, and fees, and says these contracts are not insurance. The law also allows civil penalties and includes effective date provisions.

IA-2025-SF2304.title: A bill for an act relating to certain public utilities, including the development of ratemaking principles permitted for recovery costs of certain investments in infrastructure by water and wastewater utilities and cost considerations for acquisitions of water, sanitary sewer, or storm water utilities.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by President and Speaker, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, passed on file.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.

IA-2025-SF2304.aiSummary: Became law in Iowa. It lets water and wastewater utilities seek special rate charges to recover costs for certain infrastructure work, such as new required facilities, relocations, and other nonrevenue projects needed for health, safety, resilience, or environmental protection. Utilities must first get commission approval for a plan, and the law sets filing, review, and cost limit rules for those charges.

IA-2025-HF2231.title: A bill for an act establishing a seal of civics excellence program administered by the department of education to recognize student excellence in civics.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, attached to SF 2361.

IA-2025-HF2231.aiSummary: The law creates a seal of civics excellence program run by the state education department. It lets high school students earn a seal by showing knowledge of American government and taking part in civic and community activities. Schools may join the program if they choose, and the seal can be put on a transcript or diploma. The department may charge a small fee for printing and postage.

IA-2025-SF2289.policyArea: building codes, gambling, homeland security and emergency management department
IA-2025-SF2289.aiSummary: The act changes rules for gambling, state building codes, and certain residential care facilities. It lets the state gambling commission take more enforcement steps, changes some tax withholding rules on gambling winnings, and says part of that tax change takes effect right away. It also updates rules for safe rooms and storm shelters in the building code, and creates a special class of residential care facilities for pediatric palliative care patients that only provide respite care and hospice services.
